comment: Named energy-recovery PRODUCT profiles. #217.
These are equipment characteristics, not code requirements. NECB's own
numbers deliberately live elsewhere: 5.2.10.1.(4)'s 50% enthalpy minimum
and 5.2.10.1.(6)'s overshoot control are applied on the reference path by
btap/codes/necb/hvac/energy_recovery.py, and Table 5.2.10.4's 65/55/45%
by design temperature is a CSA C439 dwelling-unit rating condition. Putting
any of those here would recreate the #183 defect, where btap.modeling
acquired 37 embedded NECB-derived values because no boundary stopped it.
The pinned gem's own default row, NECB_Default_All at 0.5/0.5, IS that 50%
minimum, which is exactly why it is not reproduced as a default here.
Keyed by CORE x TRANSFER, not by core alone. The catalogue already ships a
plate HRV at latent 0.0, and the device's own name is derived from whether
latent > 0 (energy_recovery.py, canonical.py), so a single 'plate' profile
carrying latent 0.564 would contradict that row's name. A plate core can be
sensible-only (HRV) or an enthalpy membrane (ERV); they are different
products with different frost behaviour.
`erv_profile`, or supplies all eleven `erv_*` values itself. `needs_erv:
true` alone is refused, because effectiveness, frost control and parasitic
power cannot be inferred from a boolean.
`default` names the profile used when a caller asks for recovery without
naming one (phylroy, 2026-11-14: a default so a user can move ahead to a
functioning HVAC, modifiable later). It is `plate_erv` because a static
plate is the common commercial ERV core and its -23.3 C threshold is the
one value in this file an outside source corroborates exactly.
A default is sound here where the SDK's was not, and the difference is
disclosure, not generosity: these values are named, cited and overridable,
and the audit records which profile a build used. The SDK's defaults are
uncited and internally inconsistent — plate geometry carrying rotary-wheel
latent performance, with no frost control.
An explicit `erv_*` key still overrides, and a PARTIAL set is completed
from the profile, so a row can change one field without restating ten.
`erv_bypass_control_type` applies to the CENTRAL path only: it is set on the
outdoor-air controller, which a zone ERV does not have.

plate_erv.label: Static-plate enthalpy (membrane) ERV
source: Effectiveness and defrost: pinned openstudio-standards gem,
necb/ECMS/data/erv.json row 'Plate-All', which declares
refs: ["assumption"].
Threshold INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED: RenewAire publishes -10 F
(-23.3 C) as the frost-free limit of a static-plate ERV below 40%
indoor RH. This is the one value in the gem's set that an outside
source confirms exactly.

rotary_erv.label: Rotary enthalpy wheel ERV
source: Effectiveness: gem row 'Rotary-All' (0.75 / 0.74).
Threshold -15 C rather than the gem's -23.3 C, because a wheel is not
a static plate: Greenheck's Energy Recovery Application Manual gives
an enthalpy wheel 0 F (-17.8 C) at 20% indoor RH, 5 F (-15.0 C) at
30% and 10 F (-12.2 C) at 40%, and Lennox's commercial ERV is rated
frost-free to 5 F. -15 C is the 30% RH figure, a winter-typical indoor
humidity. NOTE the threshold RISES with indoor humidity, so a single
value is itself an approximation.

plate_hrv.label: Static-plate sensible-only HRV
source: Sensible-only: latent 0.0 BY DEFINITION — an HRV recovers heat, not
moisture, and the device's name is derived from latent > 0.
Threshold -13.3 C, NOT the -23.3 C the shipped 'plate HRV' catalogue
row carries: RenewAire states a static-plate ERV has up to an 18 F
LOWER frost threshold than a comparable HRV, so -10 F + 18 F = 8 F =
-13.3 C. The shipped row applies the ERV figure to an HRV.
That row is NOT migrated to this profile here: doing so changes its
output and needs the catalogue's five gates plus a re-freeze.
